objective: Count string-iterator items with exact case and Unicode-unit semantics using one accumulator.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: String iteration and dictionary accumulation remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Frequency tables are a practical text aggregation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Code points versus code units, literal preservation and accumulator cost transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The prompt explains the Unicode model rather than assuming visual-character segmentation.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Unit and case checks prevent modest text-counting errors.

defects: The original brief did not define characters as iterator items rather than UTF-16 units or graphemes.
Code-unit splitting and lowercase normalization passed old ASCII fixtures.
The primary revealed answer copied the growing accumulator on each character, contradicting the newly explicit linear update target.
rationale: Define exact string iteration, keeping surrogate pairs together and combining marks separate without normalization or case changes. Add emoji, uppercase, punctuation, decomposed text, fresh-empty identity and many distinct characters. Replace the copy-on-each-step reference with an in-place accumulator update; junior and senior already update one accumulator. This cost review is structural reasoning, not a timing proof.

objective: Count decimal digits of a safe nonnegative integer using a loop that runs for zero.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Safe integers, Math.floor and do-while remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Digit counting is chiefly a loop lesson, so utility is one.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Zero handling, bounded domains and floating boundary errors transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The safe-integer scope makes numeric iteration exact and finite.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Power-of-ten checks prevent modest off-by-one mistakes.

defects: The whole-number domain lacked a finite safe-integer upper bound.
Original checks accepted a rounded-logarithm digit formula near untested boundaries.
A table of every old test input passed the finite old suite.
rationale: Restrict the task to nonnegative safe integers and define numeric -0 as zero. Add the largest safe integer, values at and just below a large power of ten and an unseen ordinary input. The target is logarithmic in numeric magnitude for positive n, with zero constant; this differs from representation-length complexity and is stated explicitly. Original repeated-division variants and an independent decimal-string alternative pass; unknown structural estimates keep 25 XP.
